summary: Built and registered the execution that closes the registered client-change gap. The successor experiment's new client_change_on_reconstruction case collapses a three-voter cluster to one voter, snapshots it, makes it three voters again, restarts only the former leader together with a fresh empty fourth instance, issues a client AddVoter with prevIndex 0 to that leader while the two peers of the committed configuration stay down, and then brings those peers back to see what they adopt. Local verification before submission: with the flag enabled the change committed — the leader ended with two voters, the added member was not part of the three-voter configuration it replaced, and both demoted peers came back with no vote and both adopted the rewritten configuration — while with the flag disabled the same node could not be leader with the others down, the change failed with "node is not the leader" and both peers kept their votes. Four comparisons are declared: the commit predicate for the flag-enabled case and its control, plus the adoption count and the premise that the added member lies outside the replaced configuration; validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt is outstanding, so no interpretation was recorded this turn, and the current account's gap for this channel stays open until that receipt is interpreted.
